selection_rationale: cand-2026-01 (Adversarial robustness of tool-augmented LLM NetOps agents) best matches identified literature gaps (G1) by directly addressing NetOps-specific adversarial risks, has high venue relevance, a reviewer verdict of “pass,” and a feasible experimental footprint under the run constraints.
unresolved_uncertainties: Adversarial-prompt coverage: whether the constructed adversarial corpus will represent realistic attacker creativity and breadth.
Simulator/verifier fidelity: extent to which the chosen deterministic simulator (e.g., Batfish-like) accurately reflects production safety predicates and composed multi-device behaviors.
Model-generalization risk: whether results from the selected hosted LLM generalize to other models or model families.
Statistical power and sample-size under high-refusal or low-event-rate conditions given API/cost limits and potential retries/errors.
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Preregister a precise adversarial-prompt generation procedure: sourcing rules, red-team heuristics, templating/obfuscation strategies, and coverage targets (types and counts).
Specify simulator/verifier implementation and safety predicates concretely (e.g., Batfish configuration, exact reachability/policy checks, ACL/route-policy predicates, and decision thresholds).
Either include at least one additional model (different vendor or size) in the experiment or explicitly constrain claims to a single-model scope and state the limitation in the preregistration.

Add formal sample-size/power calculations accounting for expected violation and refusal rates, and preregister retry/error-handling policies (API failures, rate limits, reproducible seeds, and allowed reruns).
Require use of only public or synthetic topologies and preregister topology-generation rules to avoid exposure of sensitive artifacts.
